basic_identification.full_title: Agro Textiles — Laminated High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) Woven Geomembrane for Water Proof Lining — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Textiles / Technical Textiles (approved by the Textile Division Council and finalized by the Technical Textiles for Agro-tech Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Agro-tech Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, sampling guidelines, and testing methods for laminated high-density polyethylene (HDPE) woven geomembranes—which are low-permeability synthetic liners—used for waterproof lining in civil, agricultural, and geo-environmental applications such as canals, ponds, and reservoirs to prevent water seepage and control fluid migration.

version_status_and_amendments.edition_year_of_copy: Second Revision, December 2015 (incorporating Amendment No. 1, March 2026)

amendment_slips.description: Completely substitutes the physical property criteria in Table 1, organizing geomembranes into four distinct varieties (Type I, Type II, Type III, and Type IV) based on thickness and mass. It updates referenced testing standards—including substituting IS 16635 for wide-width tensile properties instead of IS 13162 (Part 5)—and completely replaces Annex D with a newly standardized index puncture resistance test utilizing a double-bevel chisel-tipped solid steel rod. It also replaces muffle furnace testing parameters in Annex F by substituting a furnace temperature of 590 °C (previously 550 °C) and a sample mass of 3 g (previously 30 g) for carbon black and ash analysis.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Geo Textiles (Quality Control) Order, 2022' issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all laminated High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) Woven Geomembranes for waterproof lining must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India. Products fabricated exclusively for export are exempt if they conform to foreign buyers' specifications. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic polymers and technical textiles.

requirements.detail: Every roll or bundle of conforming geomembranes must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The minimum thickness of the finished geomembrane must strictly comply with the variety: Type I: Min 0.25 mm; Type II: Min 0.50 mm; Type III: Min 0.75 mm; and Type IV: Min 1.00 mm, tested per IS 7016 (Part 1/Sec 3).

The minimum mass of the finished geomembrane must satisfy the specified limits: Type I: Min 250 g/m²; Type II: Min 420 g/m²; Type III: Min 650 g/m²; and Type IV: Min 950 g/m², tested per IS 7016 (Part 1/Sec 2).
The polymer coating must contain a minimum of 2.5 percent carbon black by mass to provide superior UV light stabilization and durability during outdoor weathering, tested per IS 2530.

Puncture resistance is evaluated by clamping a specimen without tension between plates of a ring clamp with an open internal diameter of 45 mm ± 0.025 mm [2, 4]. A solid steel rod (diameter 7.92 mm ± 0.25 mm) with a flat chisel-shaped tip (thickness 0.8 mm ± 0.1 mm, tip edges rounded to 0.25 mm radius) is oriented at 45° to intercept warp and weft threads [5]. The test is executed at a machine speed of 300 mm/min ± 10 mm/min until rupture [3]. The maximum force recorded is reported as puncture resistance [2].
requirements.clause_reference: Annex D, Clauses D-1 to D-6

requirements.detail: Prior to testing puncture resistance, specimens must be conditioned in a controlled atmosphere of 65 percent ± 5 percent relative humidity and 27 °C ± 2 °C temperature until moisture equilibrium is reached, which is defined as mass increase <= 0.1% over successive weighings spaced >= 2 h apart.

requirements.requirement_type: Muffle Furnace Temperature for Ash Content (Annex F)
requirements.detail: To determine ash content and verify polymer purity, the muffle furnace must be calibrated and operated at a corrected high temperature of 590 °C (correcting the older limit of 550 °C). The test sample mass is strictly restricted to 3 g ± 0.2 g (previously 30 g ± 2 g) to ensure complete thermal digestion of organic remains.

The finished geomembrane must exhibit zero water leakage when subjected to hydrostatic pressure testing, and the heat-welded joints must maintain high seam strengths both before and after prolonged UV exposure.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 15351 : 2015 is the strict national Indian Standard safety specification governing laminated high-density polyethylene (HDPE) woven geomembranes used to line canals, reservoirs, agricultural ponds, and waste containment areas. Under the national Geo Textiles Quality Control Order (QCO), all such geomembranes sold or used in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to verify mechanical durability and seepage prevention. The standard defines four types based on thickness (0.25 mm to 1.00 mm) and mass (250 to 950 g/m²) [1]. Amendment No. 1 (March 2026) updates testing protocols, specifying wide-width strip tensile methods per IS 16635 [2], a highly detailed index puncture resistance test with a chisel-tipped solid steel rod [2, 5], and strict muffle furnace ash content evaluations at 590 °C to prevent the blending of low-grade or hazardous recycled plastic waste [3].
